title: Xabi Alonso backs Morgan Rogers to make an ‘instant impact’ at Chelsea
summary: New Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has backed record signing Morgan Rogers to make an immediate difference after his £117m move from Aston Villa. Alonso expects Rogers to adapt quickly to the team and the system ahead of the Premier League season, and highlighted the addition of centre-back Maxence Lacroix as part of Chelsea’s effort to build a more competitive squad. Goalkeeper competition also remains open with Robert Sanchez and newcomer Mike Penders in contention.
content:
Xabi Alonso has backed Chelsea’s new record signing Morgan Rogers to make an instant impact at the club and believes he will be ready to do so from the start of the domestic season.

Rogers completed a £117million move from Aston Villa last week but is not involved in the club’s pre-season tour to Australia and South-East Asia after playing for England at the World Cup. The attacker is instead due to report for training at Cobham on August 9, just a couple of weeks before Chelsea’s opening Premier League game at Fulham.

New Chelsea manager Alonso said he is eager to start working with the 24-year-old and believes Rogers can make a big difference at Stamford Bridge. "For sure, it’s a great signing," Alonso told reporters in Sydney, where his team were due to play Western Sydney Wanderers in a friendly. "In that position we needed an important player and I’m sure there were not many better options than Morgan Rogers.

"You need players who can have that almost instant impact and I am sure Morgan won’t need much time to adapt to the club, to the system, to his team-mates. That was the idea that we wanted, to get a top player and Morgan is one of them."

Alonso praised Rogers’s positional flexibility: "One of his best qualities is that he is flexible. In that pocket position, close to the striker, close to our No 10, but he’s played as well on the right side, but more coming from the left. He feels he is enjoying his game, his flow, and I am sure he will have good connections with the other players around him.

"If we get those connections right, that will be a great step forward in the quality of our game."

Chelsea were also close to officially announcing the £52m signing of centre-back Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace, with terms agreed and the France international set to sign a six-year deal after completing a medical. Alonso said the additions of experienced and high-quality players were central to Chelsea’s plans to improve on last season, when the club finished 10th and missed out on European qualification.

"We want to build a competitive team. We are in that process. We have great quality, great talent, and we need to know what it takes to compete in the Premier League," Alonso added. "We want a squad with the right balance between quality and mentality. Those things need to match in terms of maturity stage, where you are in your career, the moment that this point is coming for each player, the hunger, the desire, the commitment."

Alonso also declined to confirm whether Robert Sanchez will start the campaign as his first-choice goalkeeper, with Belgium international Mike Penders—impressive on loan at Strasbourg last term—having joined the squad and creating fresh competition. Penders was also on a post-World Cup break and had yet to join training.

"All the positions, everything is open. The competition within the squad is positive and I like that," Alonso said, underlining the manager’s intent to assess options ahead of the new season.
